CogniFocus and AppBlock both block distracting apps, but AppBlock works through profiles and location triggers while CogniFocus reacts the moment you drift during a session. AppBlock is a rules engine Ã¢â‚¬â€ CogniFocus is a real-time accountability system.

AppBlock: Straightforward Blocking

AppBlock is useful when your main goal is to prevent app access during a session and keep the setup simple.

That makes it appealing for users who prefer a blocker-first workflow and do not need a more animated or gamified focus loop.

CogniFocus: Blocking With Reaction

CogniFocus combines blocking with immediate feedback, recovery nudges, and visible session progress.

The session feels more alive, which can help people who need the app itself to respond when attention slips.

CogniFocus vs AppBlock: Quick Comparison

Feature CogniFocus AppBlock
Primary approach Reactive focus sessions with blocking, recovery, and progress tracking. Simple blocker-first Android workflow.
App switching support Designed to react when the distraction moment happens. Helps reduce access to distracting apps during the session.
Motivation style Goblin feedback, streaks, and XP make the session feel alive. Usually more utilitarian and direct.
Recovery after slips Built around nudges that pull you back into focus fast. Focuses more on blocking than on recovery loops.
Best for Users who need blocking plus reactive accountability. Users who want a more direct blocker and a cleaner interface.

Which One Should You Choose?

Choose AppBlock if you want a plain Android blocker and do not need rewards or reactive feedback.

Choose CogniFocus if you want the app to react, recover, and reinforce focus during the session.

FAQ

Is CogniFocus more reactive than AppBlock?

Yes. CogniFocus is built around a live focus loop with feedback and recovery, not just blocking.

Does AppBlock work for simple distraction blocking?

Yes. AppBlock is a reasonable choice if you want a straightforward Android blocker workflow.

Which one is better for app switching?

CogniFocus is the stronger fit if your main problem is app switching during focus sessions.

Blocking is step one. Reacting is step two.
